findings.highlight: my neck is stiff
findings.evidenceJa: 首のあたりが妙に重かった
findings.governingReading: The area around Shirou’s neck feels strangely heavy.
findings.explanation: The English prematurely diagnoses stiffness before the next page explains the heavy sensation through tight shoulders.

findings.highlight: the bright sunlight
findings.evidenceJa: 障子ごしの陽射し
findings.governingReading: sunlight filtering through the shoji
findings.explanation: The room-specific filtered light becomes generic bright sunlight.

findings.highlight: it hurts when I suddenly move
findings.evidenceJa: 殴られた個所が疼く
findings.governingReading: the spot on his abdomen that was struck throbs when he moves suddenly
findings.explanation: The English omits both the prior blow and the localized throbbing it causes.

findings.highlight: your body’s tired
findings.evidenceJa: 疲れも溜まってる
findings.governingReading: fatigue has probably been building up too
findings.explanation: The accumulated burden Sakura notices becomes a generic present bodily state.

findings.highlight: I nod and head into the hallway
findings.evidenceJa: 居間を通り過ぎて廊下に向かった
findings.governingReading: He nods, passes through the living room, and heads for the hallway.
findings.explanation: The English omits Shirou passing Sakura in the living room, weakening the spatial setup for his realization and return.

findings.highlight: this is just like[line3]
findings.evidenceJa: 今のは何処か[line3]
findings.governingReading: There was something somehow off about what just happened.
findings.explanation: The English invents an unfinished comparison rather than Shirou’s dawning sense that something is wrong.

findings.highlight: she slowly raises her upper body
findings.evidenceJa: けだるい仕草でゆっくりと体を起こしていた
findings.governingReading: Sakura slowly raises herself with languid, listless movements.
findings.explanation: The English removes the visible lethargy that contradicts her earlier energy.

findings.highlight: She must have come to her senses
findings.evidenceJa: 支えられてようやく気がついたのか
findings.governingReading: Perhaps only when supported did Sakura finally notice Shirou.
findings.explanation: The English implies Sakura regained consciousness although she was already moving and speaking-capable.

findings.highlight: She smiles and brushes my hand off of her
findings.evidenceJa: にこやかに言って手をほどく
findings.governingReading: Sakura says it cheerfully and gently disengages his supporting hand.
findings.explanation: The English makes Sakura’s withdrawal sound dismissive or irritated rather than pleasantly self-effacing.

findings.highlight: she doesn’t notice she’s sick
findings.evidenceJa: 自分の熱に気がついていない
findings.governingReading: she seems unaware of her own feverish heat
findings.explanation: The English broadens one concrete symptom into complete ignorance of being ill.

findings.highlight: I can’t care for Sakura’s health
findings.evidenceJa: 桜の容体に気を配れない
findings.governingReading: being unable to pay attention to Sakura’s condition
findings.explanation: The English can imply lack of care or caregiving rather than Shirou’s failure to notice and monitor her condition.

findings.highlight: I pull her into the living room
findings.evidenceJa: 客間に向かう
findings.governingReading: He takes her by the hand toward the guest room.
findings.explanation: The English sends them to the living room instead of the guest room where Shirou intends Sakura to lie down.

findings.highlight: All her energy must have been a result of the fever
findings.evidenceJa: 熱でぼーっとしていた物だったのか
findings.governingReading: Her unusually high morning spirits may have come from being dazed by fever.
findings.explanation: The English makes fever generate energy and removes Sakura’s impaired, foggy awareness.

findings.highlight: I’ll be fine
findings.evidenceJa: 元気だからな
findings.governingReading: Shirou is healthy or functional despite being injured.
findings.explanation: The English shifts Shirou’s claim about his present fitness into a prediction of future recovery.

findings.highlight: I don’t have such liberty
findings.evidenceJa: 学校に行く余裕なんかない
findings.governingReading: He has no practical or mental leeway to attend school after losing Saber.
findings.explanation: The English makes incapacity sound like lacking permission or freedom.

findings.highlight: you can rest once in a while
findings.evidenceJa: たまには派手に休んでもいい
findings.governingReading: Once in a while Sakura may take a conspicuous, thorough day off.
findings.explanation: The English removes Shirou’s playful emphasis that she can make a proper production of resting.

findings.highlight: I’m feeling perfectly fine, and you’re injured
findings.evidenceJa: 熱なんてないし
findings.governingReading: and she has no fever, while Shirou is injured
findings.explanation: The English omits Sakura’s explicit denial of the symptom Shirou just identified.

findings.highlight: She must not have the power to stand up, or maybe she can’t stand up because her body is heavy
findings.evidenceJa: 桜には立つ力がないのか、こんなにも体が重くなったから立てなくなったのか
findings.governingReading: Whether Sakura lacks the strength to stand, or whether her body has become so heavy that she cannot stand.
findings.explanation: The first of Shirou’s two uncertain explanations is promoted to “must,” making his observation more certain than it is.

findings.highlight: if you use up extra energy
findings.evidenceJa: 無駄に体力使ったら
findings.governingReading: if she needlessly expends her physical strength
findings.explanation: The English changes wasteful expenditure of stamina into using some supposed surplus “extra energy.”

findings.highlight: Delirious, Sakura
findings.evidenceJa: うわごとのように桜は言う
findings.governingReading: Sakura speaks as though in delirium.
findings.explanation: The English promotes Shirou’s comparison of her speech to delirium into a diagnosed state.

findings.highlight: takes a firm grip on my arm
findings.evidenceJa: 一度だけ、抱えた俺の腕をしっかりと握ってきた
findings.governingReading: She firmly grips the arm holding her only once.
findings.explanation: The English omits the singular, fleeting nature of Sakura’s contact.

findings.highlight: heaving breasts
findings.evidenceJa: 呼吸の度に苦しげに上がる胸
findings.governingReading: her chest rising painfully with each breath
findings.explanation: The mature branch replaces clinical respiratory distress with sexualized anatomy and drops the pain.

findings.highlight: go get some medicine
findings.evidenceJa: 風邪薬でも処方してもらえばいい
findings.governingReading: have a doctor prescribe cold medicine or the like
findings.explanation: The English removes both the prescription and Shirou’s specific assumption that Sakura has a cold.

findings.highlight: I leave the guest room
findings.evidenceJa: 今度こそ客間を後にする
findings.governingReading: This time, Shirou really does leave the guest room.
findings.explanation: The English removes the contrast with his earlier aborted departure, weakening the timing of Sakura’s final murmur.

findings.highlight: feverish tones
findings.evidenceJa: 熱にうかされた声
findings.governingReading: a voice delirious with fever
findings.explanation: The English turns impaired fever speech into a stylistic tone.

findings.highlight: they are a large family
findings.evidenceJa: とにかく大所帯なのだ
findings.governingReading: It is, in any event, a very large household or operation.
findings.explanation: The English calls the many intimidating “employees” one literal family, flattening the Fujimura organization joke.
